claims.statement: For every m>=1 and every p satisfying x(T_m)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T_m)+1, the complete ordinary favorable-leaf sum S(T_m,p) is strictly negative.
claims.scope: Only the ordinary trees T_m consisting of path a-b-r with m centers adjacent to r, each center having three private leaves; original leaves and the fixed strict selector are used. The proof uses the admitted forest descent bound n<=4x from the C5 common handoff and an exact finite Python base for m=3..999, with algebraic estimates for m>=1000. It makes no assertion for arbitrary trees.
claims.reason: The central strict LC and mixed-minor inequalities are derived for m>=1000, and all stated finite-base margins plus eligible selector/full-sum rows are independently replayed with exact integers. The family consequence follows from the C5 handoff's admitted forest descent bound. The finite base is computer-assisted and not kernel checked; this is a family result only, not a verdict on the registered all-tree primary.

limitations: The result is restricted to the specified T_m family and does not settle the all-tree lower-region aggregate.
The finite base is exact Python arithmetic, not a Lean/kernel certificate.
The all-m selector bridge depends on the forest descent bound supplied by the C5 common handoff; this route does not reprove that separate result.
